confirmed_facts: HSBC maintains an active Quantum Technologies team within Emerging Technology, Innovation and Ventures.

inferred_risks: INFERRED: HSBC has not publicly named the exact PQC algorithms (e.g. ML-KEM-768/1024 or ML-DSA-65/87) utilized in the Quantinuum pilot.
INFERRED: Core transaction banking and high-value payments (CHAPS, SWIFT) remain on classical encryption (RSA/ECDSA) without a published cutover date.
INFERRED: Long-dated OTC derivatives, trade finance records, and custody records held by HSBC are exposed to Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later (HNDL) risk.
INFERRED: HSBC's innovation pilot with Quantinuum does not equate to an enterprise-wide production deployment across core clearing systems.

active_migration_requirement_assessment.analysis: HSBC has an active institutional initiative exploring quantum-safe cryptography and defensive architectures, but it is currently scoped within Emerging Technology R&D and pilot programs (Quantinuum, IBM). There is no active commercial RFP or public regulatory mandate requiring immediate production rail cutover.

source_urls.title: Applied Research — J.P. Morgan
exact_excerpts: Exploring the frontiers of Quantum Technologies as they are applied to the business, covering Quantum Computing and Quantum-Secured Communications, to address Quantum Computing’s inevitable disruption to today's cryptography.

We research and develop new solutions in emerging technologies like quantum networking, quantum-safe cryptography, silicon photonics, and decentralized systems to ensure JPMorganChase stays ahead of the curve in technology.

For example, the Networking and Security R&D Team at Global Technology Applied Research is leading research efforts in quantum networking and quantum-safe cryptography, which aim to address future risks of quantum computing attacks.
Also, in preparation for the arrival of cryptographically relevant quantum computers, the team is conducting research into methods to adapt blockchain technologies to be quantum resistant.

inferred_risks: INFERRED: JPMC's blockchain networks (Onyx / Kinexys) rely on classical elliptic curve cryptography (secp256k1) vulnerable to Shor's algorithm.
INFERRED: JPMC has not disclosed a specific quantum-resistant algorithm stack (e.g. ML-DSA vs stateful hash signatures) or migration cutover timeline for digital assets.
INFERRED: JPMC's Applied Research initiatives represent internal exploratory scientific investigations, not active vendor procurement requests.
INFERRED: Core wholesale payments (Fedwire, CHIPS, Clearing House) remain on classical cryptographic rails without published migration milestones.

active_migration_requirement_assessment.analysis: JPMorgan Chase demonstrates clear institutional R&D focus on quantum-safe cryptography and quantum-resistant blockchain adaptations. However, this is an internal scientific research initiative rather than a formal enterprise purchasing cycle. The need is real at the architectural evaluation and prototyping level, not at the immediate production cutover level.
